item.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Is Removing Controversial Content
item.description:
Activision is officially removing controversial video footage included in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 that was taken from the 2022 Itaewon Disaster, which resulted in 160 deaths. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 's main campaign focuses heavily on a renewed military conflict on the Korean peninsula.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

The newest entry in the beloved shooter franchise has brought plenty to excite fans of the series. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 's campaign centers on the Korean peninsula, focused on a reignited military conflict between South Korea and North Korea that design director Alex Norris called the largest campaign in Modern Warfare history. Activision also made some big changes to the Call of Duty franchise's movement systems, adding the ability to both hang and shimmy from ledges and pipes. Now, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is officially removing some of the most controversial content in the game.

Call of Duty: MW4 Issues New Statement on Cheaters

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 issues a new official statement addressing the state of cheating in the game.

By Daniel Morris

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Removing Itaewon Disaster Footage

Activision officially made a statement in response to backlash regarding the inclusion of Itaewon Disaster footage in Modern Warfare 4 . A spokesperson for the company issued a public apology for the use of the traumatic footage and said that it did not "intend to reference or trivialize the Itaewon Disaster" with its inclusion. Activision expressed its sympathy to the affected families and that the footage's original intent was to provide a "realistic and immersive experience," not to reference a real-world tragedy. Activision is expected to remove the Itaewon Disaster footage from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 in an update on November 12.

The decision to remove the Itaewon Disaster footage from Modern Warfare 4 comes as Activision has previously addressed potential issues with the setting. The company consulted a variety of authorities to accurately represent the conflict on the Korean peninsula, including defectors from North Korea and Korean employees working at Infinity Ward. Longtime Call of Duty: Modern Warfare protagonist John Price also features prominently in the game's main campaign, with Danish actor Mads Mikkelsen cast as Modern Warfare 4 's antagonist.

The launch of Modern Warfare 4 has not been without its issues from a gameplay perspective as well. Many fans have complained about a higher time to kill in the newest Call of Duty than past games in the series, with fans feeling that it takes too long to score kills. Fans have already cited issues with performance on the Nintendo Switch 2 version of Modern Warfare 4 , experiencing significantly greater input lag on the Nintendo console than the PS5 version.

While Activision has not released official numbers for Modern Warfare 4 yet, the game has already had a strong showing on Valve's platform. Modern Warfare 4 peaked at 227,433 concurrent players on Steam within its launch window, boasting a Very Positive review score on the online marketplace. The game has notably performed better than 2025's Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 following its launch, though the game's player count still lagged behind Call of Duty: Black Ops 6 , which saw 300,000 players on release.

item.title: PlayStation 5 Officially Has 6 Big Games Releasing in November 2026
item.description:
PlayStation 5 gamers have six big games to look forward to in November 2026, with Grand Theft Auto 6 the obvious headliner. Grand Theft Auto 6 is by far one of the most highly-anticipated new game releases of all time, if not the most highly-anticipated. GTA 6 is the kind of game that has literally sold PS5 consoles, and millions will be looking forward to its release come November 19.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

But GTA 6 isn't coming alone. November 2026 is relatively sparse compared to most months, but there are still other notable new releases coming to PS5. These new games may lack the hype that GTA 6 has behind it, but there is something for just about every kind of gamer with the November 2026 lineup.

2 PS5 Games Are Being Delisted on December 31

Two games released in 2019 and 2021 are getting delisted from the PlayStation 5 and a handful of other platforms on December 31.

By Dominik Bošnjak

List of New PS5 Games Releasing in November 2026

  • Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered - November 3
  • Zero Parades: Director's Cut - November 3
  • Void/Breaker - November 4
  • DreamWorks Shrek 2: Remastered - November 10
  • Barbie Rewind - November 12
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 - November 19

Kicking things off for the PS5 in November 2026 is Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered on November 3, which will be joined by Zero Parades: Director's Cut . November 4 will see the release of Void/Breaker , and DreamWorks Shrek 2: Remastered is coming on November 10. Barbie Rewind will hit the scene on November 12, and finally, Grand Theft Auto 6 will release to the masses on November 19. Nothing can really compete with GTA 6 , but if you are looking for something to help tide you over, then the other new PS5 games releasing in November might be able to help.

For those unfamiliar with the other games, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is an enhanced version of the classic OG Xbox fighting game that pits various Godzilla franchise monsters against each other. It's releasing the same week as the new movie Godzilla: Minus Zero , so it should be a big few days for Godzilla fans.

Upcoming Releases

Zero Parades: Director's Cut is the long-awaited PS5 version of the Disco Elysium -style RPG, while Void/Breaker is the 1.0 release of a roguelite FPS that has enjoyed a great deal of acclaim in early access. Shrek 2: Remastered is, as its name implies, the remastered version of the old-school Shrek 2 video game, complete with 4-player local co-op. Barbie Rewind , meanwhile, is a collection of classic Barbie games. Those nostalgic for these older games will especially have a lot to look forward to in November.

GTA 6 is set to be the biggest new release of the year, and it alone will ensure that November 2026 is one to remember for PS5 gamers.

item.title: 6 Near-Perfect Atari 2600 Games Nobody Remembers, Ranked
item.description:
Ah, the Atari 2600 , an important console with a complicated legacy that involves some of gaming's earliest high and lowlights. Except for a couple of ports like Pac-Man and legendary disasters like E.T. (which isn't a bad game), I imagine most people are not only unfamiliar with the platform's library, but also have played none of its offerings. Atari 2600 games are way too old-school to be haphazardly recommended, and most retro articles tend to skip forward to the NES.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

The thing is, the Atari 2600's best games are basically stripped-down arcade romps that excel because of their simplicity rather than in spite of it . Yes, the console had a serious quality control issue that ultimately led to the 1983 video game crash, but its masterpieces hold up shockingly well and deserve to be remembered for what they accomplished.

I'm sticking to games that are still fun to play today, even if just for about 15 minutes.

6 Dragonstomper Was The First True RPG On Consoles

The Atari 2600's Turn-Based RPG Before Dragon Quest

  • Very ambitious for the hardware.
  • Required the use of the Starpath Supercharger.

That's right, Dragon Quest wasn't the first turn-based RPG with "Dragon" in the title, as Starpath's Dragonstomper was released all the way back in 1982. Generally regarded as the first console role-playing game, this title contains quite a few staples of the genre: random encounters, turn-based combat with RNG, dropped items, and stats. Yes, the visuals are extremely plain, but they are also incredibly obvious what they are trying to represent.

Find the odd one out before the timer hits zero.

While the above pictures only showcase the first act, Dragonstomper is divided into three segments that actually change things up quite a bit . The first act is mostly just exploration, random battles, stat grinding, and resource gathering; meanwhile, act 2 moves to a village, introduces shops and a merchant system, and drops combat entirely. Finally, act 3 heads into a dungeon containing the final boss, bringing everything together nicely.

Don't get me wrong, Dragon Quest is far superior and more important for JRPGs, but Dragonstomper was a nice step in that direction.

5 Entombed Is Atari 2600 Magic

An Endless Dungeon That Defies Hardware

  • A maze survival game with a map that shouldn't have been possible on the Atari 2600.

OK, we are getting into technical territory now, and I'm not going to pretend I fully understand the wizardry on display here. Entombed challenges you to survive a maze that continuously scrolls upwards, one that could lead to brick walls or zombies. As an idea, this might not sound too complex, but the Atari 2600's 128 bytes of RAM wasn't actually capable of storing an endless scrolling dungeon, and random generation would result in too many unfair dead ends to work as a solution.

Entombed 's developers, Western Technologies, figured out a workaround where the maze generates blocks depending on the surrounding context, so it decides whether to add a wall or an open path. That's a very simple explanation of things, but I believe that is the gist of the matter. Honestly, none of that really matters, as Entombed is just a fun way to spend a few minutes .

6 Near-Perfect NES Games Nobody Played

The Nintendo Entertainment System had plenty of massive hits, along with plenty of fantastic games that nobody played in North America.

10
By Mark Sammut

4 Pressure Cooker Is Activision At Its Best

Get Ready To Plate Some Burgers!

  • Ancestor to modern plate-assembly games.

Some folks might not know this, but Activision was on fire during the Atari 2600 days , releasing a few of gaming's earliest masterpieces ( Kaboom , Pitfall , and River Raid , just to name a few). Pressure Cooker came out right at the end of the publisher's hot streak on the console, but 1983 wasn't exactly a great year to release a new game.

Mechanically speaking, Pressure Cooker sits as one of the most complete games on the Atari 2600, and its core gameplay loop is very similar to modern kitchen panic games like Overcooked . You play a chef who has to assemble burgers based on customer orders, a process that involves picking the right toppings, crafting the final burger, and sending it down the right conveyor belt. Naturally, a timer constantly ticks away to ensure players are always on edge.

Of all the Atari 2600 games in this article, I enjoy replaying Pressure Cooker the most.

3 ​​​​​​​Beamrider Brought Pseudo-3D To The Atari 2600

Making The Most Of Very Little

  • Developers are just the best.

You know what, let's stick with Activision for one more game, although Beamrider was developed by David Rolfe, Action Graphics, and Cheshire Engineering (for the Atari 2600 port). The console couldn't depict perspective and depth, as there was only so much its 1977 chip could accomplish; yet, Beamrider somehow gives off the impression of 3D . I mean, a very primitive and basic 3D, but 3D nevertheless.

Across five lanes, players must perfectly align themselves with their target to strike a direct hit, with the goal being to destroy 15 standard enemies to clear a sector and summon a boss. Enemies generally move down these lanes, and they gradually become bigger as they near, creating the illusion of 3D movement. The space shooter looks perfect for the era, and it also plays pretty darn well.

10 Near-Perfect 1990s Video Games That No One Remembers

The 1990s was a wonderful era for games, but some great examples have been forgotten.

1
By Chris Littlechild

2 Turmoil Is Pure Atari 2600 Goodness

Nothing Complex, And That's Perfectly Fine

  • A classic points game.

Turmoil is a flawless arcade experience on home console. The concept is very straightforward: move a ship across seven lanes, switch directions, and shoot everything that moves. Some targets go down easily, while others move at a blistering pace or need to be shot in the back. Collect points, survive an onslaught, and try not to blow up.

Honestly, I don't have too much to say about Turmoil . Like so many Atari 2600 classics, the game executes one core idea really well , and the replayability comes from trying to outdo your previous score. Simple but great.

1 Solaris Is A Space Epic Like No Other

The Atari 2600 Could Be Depth

I don't believe I'm going to say this about an Atari 2600 game of all things, but I initially had no idea what I was meant to do in Solaris . Developed by Atari, this 1986 release basically served as the console's swan song, even if it wasn't technically the final game released on the system. By this point, the Atari 2600 was nearly a decade old and very much a non-factor culturally; however, the console actually had a very good commercial run towards the end of the 1980s, so it wasn't exactly dead either.

Solaris is complex, and I don't mean just compared to other Atari 2600 titles . You pilot a starship in a galaxy ruled by the Zylon, and your goal is to deliver humans to a planet called Solaris. You do this by picking a sector from a 16x16 map, warping correctly, picking up survivors, fighting off Zylon enemies, bombing planets held by the enemy, and finding space stations. The game throws a lot at you, and it can be hard to appreciate when played nowadays without the instruction manual; however, there is a lot to admire here.

item.title: New Switch 2 Horror Game Proves Lethal Company's Formula Still Has Room to Grow
item.description:
It goes without saying that Lethal Company is one of the most recognizable co-op horror games ever created, and it's easy to see why. And it's probably not how much people love collecting scrap, but it seems like they love doing it when they are constantly in danger of getting killed in the process. However, even though this formula works pretty well for the game, there is always room for improvement, and it seems like R.E.P.O. is determined to prove that.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

R.E.P.O. is expected to launch on Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027, and its premise is so ridiculous that it is probably going to work like a charm. Players have to steal valuable objects from haunted locations and transport them to safety without getting killed by monsters. However, the game uses physics-based mechanics, so objects have weight, and it can be quite difficult to move them without damaging them. This is most certainly not an entirely new concept, especially for those who are familiar with Lethal Company , but R.E.P.O .'s approach might very well be ready to take the experience to the next level.

Lethal Company Developer Releases Free-to-Play Horror Game on Steam

A new psychological horror game from a well-known solo developer is now free to play on Steam, and fans of the genre should check it out.

By Mohsen Baqery

R.E.P.O. Turns an Ordinary Task Into a Chaotic Horror Experience

The idea of Lethal Company is for players to collect scrap from abandoned industrial moons to meet their company's quota. This is quite a straightforward objective, but completing it is definitely not as easy as it sounds. R.E.P.O. uses a similar approach, but instead of collecting scrap, players have to move furniture and other valuable objects. To most people, this does not sound like an important difference, but it actually changes how players relate to the experience significantly.

Find the odd one out before the timer hits zero.

After all, everyone has had to move furniture at least once at some point in their lives, so that frustrating feeling of carrying something heavy or fragile is familiar to a lot of people. On the other hand, not everyone has experienced wandering around abandoned facilities collecting scrap and discovering secrets. In other words, this is where R.E.P.O. has a significant advantage, because the experience is a lot more immersive due to its relatability. Of course, the fact that the entire premise of the game is so ordinary and ridiculous at the same time just makes it even easier to appreciate the humor.

Even though monsters are quite a big problem, R.E.P.O. players will have plenty of other things to worry about as well.

Moreover, what really has the potential to change the way players experience R.E.P.O. is that everything follows the laws of physics, so there is actually strategy involved when it comes to deciding how you are going to move certain objects. This is especially relevant to large items like dressers and beds or fragile objects like vases. In other words, collecting loot is not only about finding something valuable anymore. Moreover, players will have to coordinate directions when transporting objects, which adds another layer of complexity to the main objective of the horror game. It actually seems like even though the monsters are quite a big problem, players generally have a lot of other things to worry about as well.

Whether they like it or not, monsters also have to follow the laws of physics, which is a very interesting detail, especially considering that in most horror games, enemies are just treated like obstacles that players have to avoid. However, in R.E.P.O. , players will be able to interact with the monsters by grabbing them, lifting them off the ground, and even throwing them into other objects. This makes the physics system an important part of combat and survival as well. This can absolutely make encounters extremely unpredictable, which in turn tends to create the most memorable parts of any gaming experience.

R.E.P.O. and Lethal Company Can Succeed Without Replacing Each Other

Generally, R.E.P.O. doesn't seem to be reinventing co-op horror because Lethal Company has already demonstrated that collecting valuable objects while trying to survive is a pretty successful strategy. So, instead of drastically changing something that has been proven to be effective, R.E.P.O. has simply decided to build on what made it so special and entertaining in the first place. What's even more interesting is that Lethal Company and R.E.P.O. don't necessarily have to compete for the exact same audience either.

How to Use the Leaf Blower in REPO
How to Use Staffs in REPO
Where to Find the Secret Shops in REPO
How to Get & Use Vehicles in REPO

People who enjoy the tension of meeting quotas while trying to survive can appreciate both games, but since the two titles approach gameplay differently, there are also plenty of reasons to choose one over the other. In other words, experimenting with the same successful formula often gives co-op fans more variety without having to force them to abandon the type of experience they already enjoy.

R.E.P.O.

item.title: Final Fantasy Resonance: How to Find and Beat Ultima Weapon
item.description:
The Ultima Weapon has been in the series long before Final Fantasy Resonance . It does not always present itself in the same way, and it has multiple variations of it across several games. Even games that are not strictly Final Fantasy , such as Kingdom Hearts , have some form of it. This guide goes over how to find and beat the Ultima Weapon in Final Fantasy Resonance .

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover
Final Fantasy Resonance: How to Get All Legendary Arms

Want to know where to find the legendary gear in Final Fantasy Resonance? Then check this guide out for all the details.

By Steve Booker

How to Find the Ultima Weapon

Before you can even attempt the Ultima Weapon, you must complete the entire main story first . That means finishing all main quests for all 8 chapters.

After you have beaten the game, you can save clear data. Once you load the clear data, you will start on the airship before the point of no return in the main quest.

You will get extra dialogue that hints toward the Ultima Weapon in a huge crater. You will find the Ultima Weapon in the Ardra Crater . If you look on the world map, it is a dark crater to the south-east of the Zoldaad continent. You are able to go there before completing the game, but nothing happens.

When you go to the crater after loading clear data, you will see a giant machine. Land and interact with it to fight the Ultima Weapon.

How to Beat the Ultima Weapon

The Ultima Weapon is a level 70 enemy with 3.9 million HP. It also has multiple modes:

  • Physical Attack Mode
    • High Physical Attack

  • Magic Attack Mode
    • High Magic Attack

  • Healing Mode
    • Uses healing and buffs

  • Status Ailment Mode
    • Uses various status ailments

  • Tank Mode
    • Has high physical and magic defense.

It will periodically switch between the two different modes depending on the fight and its HP.

The easiest way to tell which mode you're fighting is to use Libra. One of the traits gives you a hint. For example, "Has high physical attack" is the Physical Attack mode.

Battle Tips

Ultima Weapon is a very high level, and you'll want to be even higher to win. This is the ultimate boss, so you'll want to have the best Visions and abilities.

Libra is extremely helpful in this fight because of how often Ultima Weapon shifts modes. Lid also makes the fight much easier by using her Mechamog Scan ability. This will implant a random weakness in the Ultima Weapon in addition to the ones it cycles through during the fight. The weakness will also stay, so you won't need to worry about changing it if you get a favorable weakness.

Fina and/or Nichol help a lot with healing and buffs. Fina can save the fight by using her 2nd Limit Break to completely heal and revive all allies.

Watch out for when Ultima Weapon purges buffs because you'll need to reapply everything again when using Nichol.

High damaging magic attackers like Sakura and Archwitch Fina also help. Since Ultima Weapon has a ton of HP, you'll want them to constantly hit with 100k or more damage on their turns.

Here is an ideal setup to defeat Ultima Weapon:

  • Lid (Debuff Tank)
    • Wilhelm Vision, Spirit of Charlotte, WoL, and Sephiroth/Cecil

  • Fina (Healer)
    • Ayaka Vision, Spirit of Shantotto and Charlotte

  • Archwitch Fina (Magic Damage Dealer)
    • Amelia Vision, Spirit of Shantotto, Victora, and Terra

  • Nichol (Buffer/Magic Damage)
    • Shantotto Vision, Spirit of Terra, Leah, and Y'shtola

Even though Rain makes for the better tank, Lid can still get high HP and defenses. Her mechabo abilities are also incredibly valuable, so you get room for another party member by having Lid take on the Sentinel role and tank.

Nichol will spend most of his time keeping his Formation buffs active for maximum damage, stagger, and defense. Occasionally, he can use Faith on Archwitch Fina, dispel the buffs from Ultima Weapon, or apply debuffs to increase Archwitch Fina's damage.

Fina will mostly heal and summon either Bahamut or an Esper that matches the elemental weakness.

Archwitch Fina will want to use Witching Hour for increased damage, then spam Dualcast her strongest magic. It is ideal if Fire or Earth weakness is added since she's using Amelia. Using Dualcast on Amelia's Firaga or Stonega has a chance to activate each spell for an additional time. This means up to 4 Firagas or Stonegas.

Reward for Defeating Ultima Weapon

If you manage to take down Ultima Weapon, you will get the achievement, see an extra cutscene, and receive the Ultima Reactor accessory.

The Ultima Reactor increases stagger power and damage dealt, scaling with current HP. This is a great one to use for Rain, Lid, or Lasswell.
